@graph.name: tools
@graph.summary: Tool definitions — themselves nodes in the KG, per the repo taxonomy.

@graph.name: skills
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Skills: the instructions an Actor follows to carry out a Task.

@graph.name: processes
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Processes: BPMN diagrams that coordinate Tasks, and the decision tables their gateways compute from.

@graph.name: scenarios
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Roles: the responsibilities an Actor takes on, and who takes them on.

@graph.name: docs
@graph.summary: Documentation ABOUT the knowledge graph — how the harness works, what its directories hold, how a process runs. Rendered by the plain just-the-docs pipeline. Distinct from `folio`, which is content an author CREATES using the graph; the difference is the SUBJECT, not the format. An L1 library's catalogue is `library/`; a note about it is a `folio`; the page explaining how ingestion works is `docs`.

@graph.name: schemas
@graph.summary: A Subgraph of Node Schemas: files that state the shape other files must have.

@graph.name: qa
@graph.summary: QA verdicts and their projections — kg-qa audits, block and translation QA, qa-witness documents for the docs site, the viewer-navbar audit, result roll-ups and test runs; every `$schema` family is named in `nodeSchemas`, which is the list — a count here would be a second one, and it was already wrong by one before `viewer-nav-qa/v1` was added. Generated; never hand-edited.

@graph.name: health
@graph.summary: Repository health reports — one `health-report/v1` document per sweep, carrying every check's three-state verdict, the thresholds it applied and the basis each threshold was chosen on. Generated by `test/health/run.ts`; never hand-edited.

@graph.name: attestations
@graph.summary: QA attestations — the judgements a QA family carries across runs (pair attestations, voice reviews, agent and human verdicts, bibliography verifications and human reviews), one `qa-attestations/v1` file per subject, mirroring the derived family's tree. Kept on main where deleting derived results cannot reach them; each entry pins the hash it attested, so a stale one is detectable.

@graph.name: code
@graph.summary: Source code -- the modules, scripts and entry points an instance holds. Declared so that code is scannable at all: an undeclared file is one no checker has a reason to look at. Being declared here says nothing about whether a Tool node claims it, which is a separate question and a separate axis.

@graph.name: library
@graph.summary: L1 source content — one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested document, holding `sections/*.md`, `structure.json` and, where the source was scanned, `ocr/page-NNN.txt`. Every knowledge-graph reference to a source resolves through here, never to a loose path or a bare URL.

@graph.name: software-library
@graph.summary: Outside libraries a layer imports or vendors -- one generated `software-library` node per library per layer, with the version and sha512 its `bun.lock` pins, its SPDX licence, its range, whether it is a dev dependency, the files that import it and the shim that types it. Shares its core with `tool-release`.

@graph.name: voices
@graph.summary: Editorial voice profiles — one JSON each, carrying `"$schema": "folio-voice/v1"`. Every rule cites the ingested source or KG node it was derived from. Opt-in per folio.

@graph.name: themes
@graph.summary: Themes derived from an instance's own sources — one Theme node each, carrying `kind: sticky | webpage | publication`. The palette vocabulary is shared across every kind and only the geometry varies; every value cites where it was measured.

@graph.name: translation-sources
@graph.summary: POT templates, PO catalogues and their `TranslationNode` manifests, one directory per target locale. The INPUT to injection; the rendered output is ordinary content that declares its own `lang`.

@graph.name: folio
@graph.summary: Authored content, rendered to a website by the just-the-docs pipeline.

@graph.name: catalogue
@graph.summary: A remote catalogue modelled by reference — communities, collections and items of a corpus the layer does not hold. Every node declares whether its bytes are here (`materialized`), elsewhere (`referenced`) or unestablished (`unknown`), with no default. Distinct from `library`, which is content that IS here.

@graph.name: glossary
@graph.summary: SKOS terms (folio-glossary/v1): local terms with definitions and codes, linked to external SKOS schemes by exactMatch rather than copied. Rendered on the glossary/ page.

@graph.name: references
@graph.summary: Bibliographic references, one folio-reference/v1 node per work: a CSL-JSON item at `references/<key>`, the IRI every `\cite{key}` already points at, read as Dublin Core and BIBO through its JSON-LD.

@graph.title: WHO editorial style
@graph.description: The house editorial style of the World Health Organization: spelling, capitalization, eponym form, reference layout and non-discriminatory language, as set out in the WHO Editorial Style Manual. Derived rule by rule from the ingested manual; every rule cites the page it was read from.

@graph.title: WHO guideline development
@graph.description: How a WHO recommendation is worded and what must travel with it: strength, certainty, justification, remarks and a link to the evidence. Derived from the WHO handbook for guideline development, 2nd edition. This voice governs the language of normative statements, not the process that produces them — the process is the handbook's subject and belongs in a workflow, not a style rule.

@graph.title: WHO publication design (Western Pacific Region)
@graph.description: The visual conventions around the prose rather than the prose itself: logo use, palette, typography, pagination and figure accessibility, as set out in the WHO Western Pacific Region publication and information products style guide. This is the one voice whose rules mostly do not touch a block's text, which is why it is a separate voice rather than more rules on who-editorial — a folio can want WHO's editorial register without WPRO's brand.

@graph.title: IRIS CDN owner
@graph.description: A person: decides the export's scope, budget and storage target. Nothing downstream widens what the owner approved.

@graph.title: IRIS CDN Exporter
@graph.description: The agent role. It plans, reviews and reports; it does not hold the signing key, and it never pushes to a WHO repository.

@graph.title: Cloudflare R2 and CDN
@graph.description: Object storage behind the CDN. Every object is named by its SHA-256 and served with an immutable cache policy; an object already present is never written again. Also serves did.json. A mechanical role, held to the contract its skills state.

@graph.title: Cloudflare git (Artifacts)
@graph.description: A git repository hosted on Cloudflare Artifacts, not GitHub. Holds the release history: BagIt tag files, signatures, the cursor, checkpoints and run reports. A mechanical role: written to, deciding nothing.

@graph.title: Release signer
@graph.description: Holds the P-256 private key (GitHub environment secret IRIS_CDN_SIGNING_JWK) and signs each changed item manifest and the release tag manifest. A mechanical role.

@graph.title: IRIS CDN verifier
@graph.description: Anyone. Resolves the key from the did:web DID document, never from the package, and checks its x5c chain up to WHO's signing key. Cannot reach it: the verdict is unknown, not verified.

@graph.title: who-iris GuidelineKG path
@graph.description: who-iris's side of the parallel GuidelineKG path (docs/optimus-kg-integration.md): the deterministic scripts that verify, diff, select, publish the work order and project the result, and the agent that adjudicates first, reviews the run and opens beans. Holds no Reducto, OpenAI or Azure key, ever. Proposed: most of its skills are not written yet, and the diagrams say so step by step.

@graph.title: Zitnik lab (GuidelineKG)
@graph.description: The Zitnik lab at Harvard, which runs GuidelineKG (mims-harvard/guideline-kg, pinned by commit) on its own Reducto and Azure OpenAI keys and publishes its result releases in its own repositories. An external party: who-iris instructs nothing here; the work order and the result release are the whole interface.

@graph.title: Human reviewer (SME or editor)
@graph.description: A person who rules on every recommendation-class or contraindication claim the two KG extractors disagree on, and on anything the agent found undecidable. The ruling is kept beside the agent's, never over it.

@graph.title: GuidelineKG result release
@graph.description: What the lab publishes per work order: guideline_kg.jsonl and a SHA-256 manifest naming the work order, the CDN release and the GuidelineKG commit. A mechanical role, held outside who-iris: read and verified, never written by who-iris.

@graph.name: who-iris-translations
@graph.description: The gettext side of who-iris's own strings, one directory per target locale: the `glossary/who-iris--who-terms` catalogues that translate this instance's WHO terms. Moved here from cat-harness/translations/ on the owner's ruling of 2026-10-04, "move things to semantically appropriate place" (bean riit): a scheme's translations sit with the instance whose terms they translate.

@graph.name: library
@graph.description: The IRIS items this instance holds rather than merely names. The three worked examples are `wpr-rdo-2020-003-eng` (the WPRO publication style guide, and the worked example whose full DSpace item record drives the `iris-dspace` skill), `who-pub-tps-931` and `9789241548960-eng`. On 2026-10-30 (who-iris#107, the owner's "pre-CDN preview") every IRIS library the harness layers had ingested moved in beside them: twelve from the DAK layer (https://github.com/litlfred/smart-base; digital health guidance such as DIIG, the two classifications of digital interventions and the digital transformation handbooks) and three from the immunizations IG (the IMMZ DAK, 9789240016514 and DDCC:VS). Those layers now cite them as `{instance: "who-iris"}`. They are the `materialized` end of the catalogue -- every other node under `catalogue/nodes/` is `referenced`, and the entries here are what a materialization actually looks like. `milnorlink` is NOT here and never was an IRIS item; it went to folio-assistant-sci (bean r1lz). The id is `library`, the CONVENTIONAL one, so this entry OVERRIDES the default rather than joining it: overrides match on id and never on path, so a distinct id at the same path yields two entries for one directory and every fan-out consumer scans it twice. Measured while doing exactly that.

@graph.name: who-iris-site
@graph.description: THE IRIS REPLICA'S HOME PAGE AND SEARCH PAGE, and nothing else of the replica. The search page (search.html, issue #196, owner 2026-11-08) mimics iris.who.int/search: its facet categories are IRIS's, and their values and counts are computed in the browser from the items the query matches. Owner, 2026-10-30: the replica's item pages duplicated the library entry pages without a locale in the URL ("i want consitent bevarioior for things nuders librayr/"), so the item, collection and community-list pages are gone and their addresses 404. The IRIS-style home stays (follow-up, option A), in every language it is built in: its held items link to their library entry pages and its communities and collections to the catalogue page. `scripts/gen-iris-pages.ts` writes it (gated by `bun run cat iris:pages:check`). On the platform's site it is what `/who-iris/` serves; on who-iris's own site the `site:home` build step also writes it at the site root, and the docs home moved to `/docs/`. History: Moved out of `library/` on 2026-09-30 (bean 2b5s) so that the corpus and its rendering are separate directories: before, the mount copied the corpus along with the pages. A page shows an item's cover by referencing `../library/<slug>-cover.png`; the build publishes exactly the files a page embeds, beside the replica, and not the directory they sit in.

@graph.name: who-iris-catalogue
@graph.description: The catalogue itself: `catalogue.json` declares the corpus and its measured size; `nodes/` holds one `folio-catalogue-node/v1` per community, collection or item; `records/` holds the `folio-dublin-core/v1` metadata an item node points at through `metadataRef`. No count is written here: `check:catalogue` prints the census, and a count in prose goes stale (AGENTS.md). Most nodes are `referenced`, against 1,057,223 files upstream, and that gap IS the point. Since 2026-10-30 this is the one home for every IRIS item the harness layers know of (who-iris#107): smart-base, smart-immunizations, smart-hiv and folio-assistant moved their IRIS libraries, intakes and PDFs here and cite them as `who-iris`. `bun run cat check:catalogue` verifies every node validates and every metadataRef, libraryId and parent path resolves; a Zod schema can require the reference and structurally cannot check the file is there.

@graph.name: who-iris-skills
@graph.description: The IRIS skills: `iris-dspace` (how IRIS uses DSpace and qualified Dublin Core, stated as checkable requirements R1–R22), `iris-rest-feed`, `iris-cdn-exporter`, `iris-cdn-signing` and `iris-oxigraph`; and, under `voices/`, the WHO style guide's three house voices, declared from within by `skills.json`. Kept thin: the Dublin Core type lives in folio-assistant-core, enumeration and subsetting in large-datasets, and OCR is a cat-harness platform tool.

@graph.name: glossary
@graph.description: The WHO glossary: folio-glossary/v1 schemes of terms the WHO publications use under more than one name -- a HOUSE rule about wording, like the style-guide voices under skills/voices/ (bean ftu0). An alternative label is recorded only where a publication STATES the equivalence, and each term cites that sentence in this instance's own library; a count or a latent-semantic cosine is never the evidence. The scheme's source is the who-guideline-development voice, so its terms are minted in this instance's namespace. Rendered on the glossary/ page and checked by check:glossary, both of which read every instance's declared glossary directory.

@graph.name: who-iris-docs
@graph.description: This instance's docs, with a viewer built by cat-harness. Declared in this instance's own file rather than in `cat-harness.json`, because `compose-docs.docsLayers` treats every docs-kind entry there as a composition layer and would overlay this instance's `index.md` onto the site's own. The directory is also mounted verbatim at `/docs/who-iris/`: the mount is a copy of the directory, the viewer an index of it, and the rail links to the viewer (`visualiserHref`).

@graph.name: who-iris-processes
@graph.description: The IRIS CDN Exporter's BPMN processes: initial load, nightly change ingest over DSpace REST, weekly reconciliation, and sign-and-publish; and the proposed GuidelineKG path (optimus-kg-nightly and its two phases, kg-tool-adjudication; docs/optimus-kg-integration.md), whose unbuilt steps say so with no-skill. Cloudflare git (Artifacts) and Cloudflare R2 + CDN are lanes: exports live on Cloudflare, and GitHub Pages only previews. Each activity names the skill that carries it out; the platform's nquads-distribution process is called, not copied. Rendered drawings: docs/assets/img/processes/.

@graph.description: `scenarios/roles.json`: the roles the IRIS CDN export processes' lanes bind (owner, exporter agent, Cloudflare R2 and CDN, Cloudflare git, release signer, verifier), and the GuidelineKG path's lanes and stores (who-iris path, Zitnik lab, human reviewer, result release). Each mechanical role inherits the harness role it specialises. Declared so the lanes resolve and the checkout's role graph sees them (folio-assistant#2781).

@graph.name: who-iris-scripts
@graph.description: The catalogue checker, the cover generator and `gen-iris-pages.ts` -- the instance-local generator `wjfu` cites as the precedent for every other one here (*"instance-local generator, static HTML, committed, gated"*). Cited as a model by another instance's bean while being undeclared itself, which is the sharpest form of the `ylj7` defect: a directory can be the corpus's own worked example and still be invisible to every consumer that walks declarations.

@graph.name: who-iris-references
@graph.description: The reference lists of the held IRIS documents, one `folio-reference/v1` node per cited work. Owner, 2026-11-11: "i want all who-iris docs that have references put into their own biblio". Written by the Tool `references-extract` (step `Task_References` of folio-assistant-core's `ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn`) from each library entry's L1 sections: keyed `<doc-id>.<section>.<n>`, `provenance: extracted`, `derivedFrom` the section file, `printed` the entry verbatim. The bibliography page lists them under the document they came from (`bibliography/library/<doc-id>/`). Regenerated, not hand-edited: re-run the tool after a section is re-derived.

@graph.name: who-iris-sources
@graph.description: Source descriptors (`folio-source-descriptor/v1`): how to ENUMERATE WHO IRIS and ask it for a SUBSET, so an agent asked for part of it is not told the API by a human every time. Moved here from large-datasets' `sources/` on 2026-10-01 (owner ruling: large-datasets dissolves into cat-harness; bean `j7ql`), because a descriptor is ABOUT one corpus and the instance that holds or catalogues that corpus owns it — the schema stays in cat-harness. Its far-apart sibling, Lean mathlib, is in folio-assistant-sci: IRIS items stand alone (`subsetIsSelfContained: true`), three identifier systems, paged REST.

@graph.name: id-lookup
@graph.description: The GENERATED prefix-sharded identifier lookup over this catalogue's REFERENCED nodes: `manifest.json` plus JSON shards keyed by id prefix, each under 64 KiB. Written by `cat-harness-tools/scripts/gen-id-lookup.ts` (`bun run cat id-lookup`, gated by `id-lookup:check`), which finds this directory by its id `id-lookup` and never by this instance's name; read by `cat-harness-tools/id-lookup/lookup.js`. Here rather than beside the generator because an instance hosts its own generated outputs (D3, bean `j7ql`, 2026-10-01). Edit the catalogue, never the shards: the generator replaces this directory whole.

@graph.name: qa
@graph.description: What auditing THIS instance produced, committed so a consumer can tell "never audited" from "audited clean" — a printed verdict cannot, which is why every QA verdict here is a sidecar. TWO kinds live here and the files declare which they are via $schema: kg-qa/v1, one per audited subject, in a tree mirroring the subject’s own path, and ONE kg-qa-manifest/v1 recording the auditor’s identity for all of them. The manifest moved here from skills/ on 2026-09-27: kg-audit.ts writes it unconditionally, so its old home created a skills/ directory holding no skills in every instance that has none. At declaration time that is 2 files across scenarios (1), skills (1). No qa-results/v1 and no witnesses: this instance runs no document build and no witness-producing computation, and declaring kinds it does not hold would be an over-claim. `qa` is a `perInstance` graph typology (graph-typology-registry.ts), because a dependent audits its OWN graph — these verdicts are about this instance’s nodes, and inheriting them would attribute one instance’s findings to another. Declared WITH its files in one commit, per bean dh4f: a declared-but-absent directory makes a consumer scan nothing and report a clean run over it.

@graph.name: attestations
@graph.description: The JUDGEMENT half of this instance's QA, on main (the qa-reports skill: derived verdicts go to the qa-reports branch, judgements stay here). Today: the untainted round-trip translation rulings of who-iris's own catalogues, one qa-attestations/v1 file per catalogue and locale under translation-qa/ (criterion translation-semantic-roundtrip), each string's ruling pinned by the hashes of the msgid and msgstr it judged. Converted losslessly on 2026-11-03 from the agents' TSVs that sat under test/results/ (owner: "1. Convert to attestations"; bean folio-assistant-7mwa), so that untracking the derived results could not lose them. scripts/translation-roundtrip-report.ts derives its qa-results/v1 report from them.

@graph.name: folio
@graph.description: Authored content of this instance itself, rendered to a website. Holds the landing sticky — the instance's own description and its onboarding links, as a page-global note rather than text composited into the backdrop.

@graph.name: who-iris-libraries

@graph.name: translation-qa-prune
@graph.title: Prune round-trip rulings of removed strings
@graph.description: Drop the translation-semantic-roundtrip rulings of strings the catalogues no longer hold, and renumber the rest to catalogue order. Rulings are paired with strings by the hash of their msgid, so removing strings invalidates none and needs no agent re-run; this is the upkeep that follows. It only drops or renumbers: a verdict is never changed or invented, and a ruling for a string the ref's history never held (one recorded ahead of its PR) is kept.

inputs.name: write
inputs.description: Apply the change to test/attestations/translation-qa/. Absent, it is a dry run that prints each dropped ruling and the renumbered spans.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.description: Whose catalogues decide what was removed. Default origin/main: the state branch serves main and every branch, so a ruling goes only once main no longer holds its string.

outputs.name: attestations
outputs.description: With --write, the rewritten `test/attestations/translation-qa/<catalogue>.<locale>.attestations.json`, to be pushed to `cat/who-iris/attestations`.
